correctness.rationale: Every consistent S lies in a Hamiltonian cycle and is either a Hamiltonian cycle or a spanning path forest. Enumerating cyclic orders and path endpoint orientations proves all compulsory links: spanning path closure, singleton-plus-path closure, three components with two singletons; other forests force no edges. Any inconsistent S contains a 3-edge star or a proper cycle; direct rules on these and n-2-vertex path premises give closure in one round. At each listed critical premise an edge is not provided by closures of any proper subpremise, forcing a distinct rule in any direct basis. Summing counts gives b_n, and the labeled exponential formula gives the closed lattice count. Independent brute intersection tested every edge subset for n=4,5,6 (64+1024+32768); exact lattice counts 8,69,647 and critical premise counts 6,75,377 matched, with all n=4,5 one-round cases checked. No finite enumeration used as infinite proof.
